During his remarks at a bilateral lunch with Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Wednesday, the president mentioned how a past visiting U.S. dignitary was treated.

“It was right here, in this very palace, that President Quezon bestowed Gen. Douglas MacArthur with a gold baton and the rank of field marshal in the Philippine Army,” Trump pointed out. “I’d like to have you do that to me, if you don’t mind. I’d love that! I mean, why the hell shouldn’t I get that?”

Some in the room laughed.

It’s not clear if Trump meant the gold baton, the rank of field marshal, or both.

Even if he made the comments in jest, the president loves honors, awards, trophies and trinkets, and has racked up quite a few of them since returning to the White House last year.

He was given a Rolex desk clock and a $130,000 gold bar from a Swiss delegation (which is now under investigation in Switzerland) and a piece of “unique” glass on a gold base from then-Apple CEO Tim Cook.

He’s also picked up awards that were made just for him, such as the “America First Award” from House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), a “Man of the Century” certificate from a Republican candidate in Iowa, and the “FIFA Peace Prize,” which the soccer body awarded Trump after his frequent complaints about not getting a Nobel Peace Prize.

He got one of those, too, although it was a secondhand honor: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, who won in 2025, gave Trump her medal when she visited the White House earlier this year.

He’s also been given everything from an “Undisputed Champion of Beautiful Clean Coal” trophy to a “McDonald’s French Fry Certification Pin.”
